title: Lift per-agent budget and timeout caps in athena.toml
summary: Per the owner's 4 Nov direction, raise the nine named values in athena.toml's [budget] and [job_plan] tables to reduce jobs ending early. Only those values change; no new keys. Audience: the owner and operators running Athena.

defaults_applied.how: Verifier runs cargo test and check-config.
Criteria check the values are read without error.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: stop budget/time caps from ending jobs early, per owner direction of 4 Nov; audience is the owner and operators.
Only athena.toml changes; defaults.toml and workflows untouched. 'Installed build' is satisfied by cargo build/test reading the repo config.
Config tests may assert on or bound budget values; if one hard-codes old values, that is a surprise to report rather than edit silently.
Line numbers read: budget values at athena.toml lines 35-42, job_plan at 212-216.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml [budget] has reader_usd = 2.00, producer_usd = 10.00, verifier_usd = 5.00, job_usd = 40.00, producer_timeout_s = 5400, verifier_timeout_s = 3600 (checkable with Grep/git diff).

git diff of athena.toml shows exactly these nine value lines changed, with no added or removed keys and no other file changed (reader_timeout_s, check_timeout_s, planner_timeout_s, critic_timeout_s stay as is).
Run `cargo test`: existing config tests pass, so the config parses without error. Run `cargo run -- check-config` (or the equivalent subcommand) and it exits without error reading the new values.
Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`; both are clean (unchanged code).

out_of_scope: Changing other timeouts (reader, check, planner, critic)
departures: Single-file value edit is smaller than typical jobs, but cold cargo test/check-config runs dominate cost.
urgent_reason: Raising the caps cuts early job endings: planners out of budget, plans out of rounds, writer and verifier timeouts.
